steps: The client stands relaxed, arms down.
Wrap the tape around the fullest part of the bust.
Keep the tape parallel to the floor, front and back.
Read the number while she breathes normally.
bust.warning: A tape pulled tight gives a smaller size, and the pattern comes out too narrow.

steps: Wrap the tape around the chest just above the bust and under the armpits.
The tape crosses the shoulder blades at the back.
Keep the tape parallel to the floor.
highBust.warning: This must be smaller than the bust measurement.

steps: Wrap the tape around the ribcage right under the bust.
Snug but not pressing, parallel to the floor.
This measurement is optional; it helps with dresses fitted under the bust.
underBust.warning: Do not let the tape sag at the back.

steps: Find the narrowest part of the torso, usually above the navel.
Wrap the tape around the waist without pulling.
She breathes normally and does not hold in her stomach.
waist.warning: A waist taken too low makes the pattern too long.

steps: The client stands with feet together.
Wrap the tape around the fullest part of the hips.
Keep the tape parallel to the floor all the way round.
hip.warning: Measure over light clothes that add no volume.

steps: Wrap the tape around the base of the neck.
It runs from below the throat to the bone that sticks out at the back.
Leave one finger of room between the tape and the neck.
neck.warning: A tight tape gives a neckline that is too small.

steps: Measure from behind while she stands straight.
Start at the tip of one shoulder and end at the tip of the other.
The tape passes over the bone at the base of the neck.
shoulderWidth.warning: Measure to the shoulder tip, not down the arm.

steps: Mark the highest point of each breast.
Measure the straight distance between the two marks.
Keep the tape level without pressing on the chest.
Find the highest point of the breast.
Measure from the top of the shoulder at the base of the neck down to that point.
Keep the tape straight, not slanted.
bustHeight.warning: Her usual bra gives a more accurate number.

steps: The arm hangs by the body with a slight bend at the elbow.
Measure from the shoulder tip over the elbow to the wrist bone.
Keep the tape laid flat along the arm.
armLength.warning: Bending the arm sharply shortens the measurement.

steps: The arm hangs relaxed by the body.
Wrap the tape around the fullest part of the upper arm.
Snug but not pressing.
upperArm.warning: The tape must not squeeze the arm.

steps: Wrap the tape around the wrist bone.
Leave one finger of room for comfort.
Keep the hand flat.
wrist.warning: If the sleeve must pass over the hand, measure around the hand too.

steps: The client stands without shoes, back against a wall.
Measure from the top of the head to the floor.
She looks straight ahead with the chin level.
height.warning: Measure without shoes so the height is not inflated.

steps: Start at the bone that sticks out at the base of the neck.
Run the tape down the spine to the waistline.
The client stands straight.
backLength.warning: The waistline is the narrowest point, not the waistband.

steps: Start at the top of the shoulder at the base of the neck.
Run the tape over the highest point of the bust down to the waistline.
Keep the tape laid flat on the body.
frontLength.warning: This is usually longer than the back length.

steps: Mark the waistline and the fullest part of the hips.
Measure straight down the side between the two.
The client stands straight.
hipDepth.warning: Measure at the side, not at the front.

steps: Mark the waistline at the side.
Measure straight down to the middle of the knee.
The client stands with feet parallel.
waistToKnee.warning: Keep the tape vertical, with no curve.

steps: Mark the waistline at the side.
Measure straight down to the floor.
The client stands without shoes.
waistToFloor.warning: Measure without shoes, and add the heel height if needed.
